links.comparator_used: Vanilla LLMs answering from training knowledge alone, with no retrieval, across four open-source LLMs on the NIDDK portion of MedQuAD
links.outcome: Quality of answers to consumer health questions (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, LLM-based evaluation and clinical validation)
links.effect: Vanilla LLMs consistently outperformed RAG variants on quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) and qualitative assessments; retrieval Precision@5 = 0.15. RAG was competitive in scientific consensus and harm reduction.
links.tradeoff: Low retrieval precision (Precision@5 = 0.15) meant RAG did not help. The authors conclude that simple retrieval and prompt engineering are not enough and that medical-specific RAG infrastructure is needed.
links.quote: Surprisingly, we find that vanilla LLM approaches consistently outperform RAG variants across both quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) and qualitative assessments.
